resumen: Verbos + to: decide, want, hope, agree, refuse; con objeto, encourage, allow, persuade, ask: She encouraged us to ask questions.
Make y let: objeto + infinitivo sin to: He made me rewrite it. They let me stay. En cambio, allow sí lleva to: They allowed me to stay.
Preposición + -ing: before installing, thanks for helping. Ojo cuando to es preposición: look forward to seeing, be/get used to driving, object to working.
Propósito: «para» + verbo se dice con to, no con for: I went to the library to borrow some books.
Stop, remember, forget, try: stop doing (dejar de) / stop to do (detenerse para); remember/forget doing (algo ya hecho) / remember/forget to do (una tarea); try doing (probar) / try to do (intentar).
Regret, go on, mean: regret to inform (lamentar comunicar) / regret doing (arrepentirse); go on doing (seguir) / go on to do (pasar a); mean doing (implicar) / mean to do (tener intención).
It's no use / worth + -ing: It's no use complaining. The museum is worth visiting. Nunca worth to visit ni doesn't worth.

preguntas.q: I really enjoy ___ to podcasts on my way to work.
preguntas.x: Enjoy va siempre seguido de -ing: I enjoy listening. No admite to + infinitivo, aunque en español digamos «disfruto escuchar».

preguntas.q: We've decided ___ a flat closer to the city centre.
preguntas.x: Decide va con to + infinitivo, como want, hope, plan o agree: We've decided to rent. Decided renting no es posible.

preguntas.q: I went to the library ___ some books for my essay.
preguntas.x: Para expresar el propósito de una acción se usa el infinitivo con to: I went to the library to borrow some books. For + verbo es un calco del español «para».

preguntas.q: Always read the instructions before ___ new software.
preguntas.x: Después de una preposición (before, after, without, for...) el verbo va en -ing: before installing. Before to install es un calco de «antes de instalar».

preguntas.q: My boss made me ___ the whole report again.
preguntas.x: Make + objeto va seguido del infinitivo sin to: made me rewrite. El to solo aparece en pasiva (I was made to rewrite it).

preguntas.a: My parents didn't allow me to stay out late.
d: My parents didn't let me to stay out late.
My parents didn't allow me stay out late.
My parents didn't let me staying out late.
preguntas.x: Allow va con objeto + to (allow me to stay), mientras que let va con objeto + infinitivo sin to (let me stay). Mezclar los dos patrones es el error más común.

preguntas.q: Our tutor encouraged us ___ questions during the lecture.
preguntas.x: Encourage, como persuade, allow o advise, va con objeto + to + infinitivo: encouraged us to ask. No admite objeto + -ing ni una oración con that detrás del objeto.

preguntas.q: I'm looking forward to ___ you at the conference next month.
preguntas.x: En look forward to la palabra to es una preposición, así que va seguida de -ing: looking forward to seeing you. Looking forward to see es el error más frecuente.

preguntas.q: Many employees objected to ___ at weekends.
preguntas.x: En object to la palabra to es preposición y pide -ing: objected to working. Por eso no puede ir seguida del infinitivo (objected to work).

preguntas.q: I stopped ___ coffee last month because it was affecting my sleep.
preguntas.x: Stop + -ing significa dejar de hacer algo: I stopped drinking coffee. Stop to drink significaría detenerse para tomar café, lo contrario de lo que se quiere decir.

preguntas.a: It's no use complaining; they won't change the rules.
d: It isn't worth to complain; they won't change the rules.
It's no use of complaining; they won't change the rules.
It doesn't worth complaining; they won't change the rules.
preguntas.x: It's no use y (not) worth van seguidos de -ing: It's no use complaining, It isn't worth complaining. Worth no es verbo, por eso no se dice doesn't worth, y no lleva to.

preguntas.q: When I moved to the UK, it took me months to get used to ___ on the left.
preguntas.x: En be/get used to (estar o acostumbrarse a) to es preposición y va con -ing: get used to driving. No hay que confundirlo con used to drive, que habla de un hábito del pasado.

preguntas.q: I clearly remember ___ the front door last night, but I forgot ___ the kitchen window, and that's how the burglar got in.
preguntas.x: Remember + -ing es recordar algo que ya hiciste (I remember locking) y forget + to es olvidar hacer algo (I forgot to close), por eso entró el ladrón. Forgot closing implicaría que sí la cerré.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'Getting up at six isn't hard for me; I've been doing it for years.'
preguntas.a: I'm used to getting up at six.
d: I used to get up at six.
I'm used to get up at six.
I get used to get up at six.
preguntas.x: Be used to + -ing significa estar acostumbrado: I'm used to getting up at six. I used to get up at six habla de un hábito pasado que ya no existe, justo lo contrario.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'As an experiment, I moved the plant to a sunnier window to see if it would grow better.'
preguntas.a: I tried moving the plant to a sunnier window.
d: I tried to move the plant to a sunnier window.
I tried move the plant to a sunnier window.
I tried for moving the plant to a sunnier window.
preguntas.x: Try + -ing es probar algo para ver qué pasa, y la acción sí se hace: I tried moving the plant. Try + to es esforzarse por hacer algo que quizá no se logró (I tried to move it, but it was too heavy).

preguntas.q: We regret ___ you that your application has been unsuccessful.
preguntas.x: Regret + to se usa para dar una mala noticia, sobre todo en lenguaje formal: We regret to inform you. Regret informing significaría arrepentirse de haber informado.

preguntas.q: After her degree in Chemistry, she worked in a lab for a few years and then went on ___ her own company, which now employs 200 people.
preguntas.x: Go on + to significa pasar a hacer algo nuevo después: went on to set up her own company. Go on + -ing significa seguir haciendo lo mismo, lo que no encaja con fundar una empresa.

preguntas.q: Accepting the job would mean ___ to another city, so I need to think about it.
preguntas.x: Mean + -ing significa implicar o suponer: would mean moving. Mean + to significa tener la intención (I meant to call you), lo que no tiene sentido con accepting the job como sujeto.
